findings.expected: MH2: every prompt includes exactly one Twist sentence with clean punctuation. withTerminalPunctuation() must not append a second terminal mark to a half that already ends in one, including when the mark sits inside a closing quote (e.g. `no survivors."`).
findings.found: withTerminalPunctuation tests only the LAST character (`/[.!?]$/`), so a twist ending in `."` fails the test and gets another '.' appended, producing a double terminal `.".`. Two data twists trigger it: src/data/finance.ts:61 ('... from "gentle nudge" to "no survivors."') and src/data/science.ts:80 ('... to pick a playful "winner."'). generate(6, {}).text ends `...a slider from "gentle nudge" to "no survivors.".`; generate(244, {}).text ends `...to pick a playful "winner.".`. The dedicated T-020 test (src/core/generate.test.ts:156) asserts only /[.!?] Twist: / and /[.!?]$/, both of which the malformed string satisfies, so the suite is green while the criterion is violated. Hit rate is ~1.4% over unfiltered seeds and ~8% over {subject:'finance',difficulty:'easy'} (seeds 0, 21, 24, 32 all reproduce).

claim.summary: All three findings fixed and verified. Fix 1 (generate.ts:25) — withTerminalPunctuation() tested only /[.!?]$/, so a twist ending in a closing quote (`no survivors."`) failed the check and got a spurious second '.' appended, producing '."'. Changed the regex to /[.!?]["')]?$/ so a terminal mark inside a trailing quote/paren is recognized. Also updated the T-020 test in generate.test.ts, which was itself asserting the same flawed /[.!?]$/ pattern (the "loophole" the finding called out that let the bug stay green) — it now uses the quote-aware regex plus an explicit not.toMatch guard against the double-terminal shape. Fix 2 (FavoritesView.tsx:106) — prompt favorite cards rendered only the raw subject/difficulty enum and never the stored timeBand. Added a DIFFICULTY_LABELS map (mirroring PromptCard.tsx) so difficulty renders as 'Medium' not 'medium', and added a new `{f.prompt.timeBand}` chip so the exact time-band label is shown, matching PromptCard's chip row. Fix 3 (BrainScoutView.tsx:75-76 / App.tsx:92) — phrase and result were component-local useState, and App unmounts BrainScoutView on every tab change, silently destroying the ladder/remixes/input with no recovery (re-scout re-rolls Math.random). Lifted `scoutPhrase`/`scoutResult` state up into App.tsx (same pattern App already uses for generator seed/filters, which do survive tab switches) and turned BrainScoutView into a controlled component (phrase, onPhraseChange, result, onResultChange props). The ladder, remixes, and typed phrase now survive switching to Favorites and back to Brain Scout. Verified each of the three verifier-provided failing cases directly against the fix (in a scratch test file, removed after confirming, not committed): generate(6,{}) and generate(244,{}) no longer produce a double terminal mark; a seeded favorite with timeBand renders it in .fav-item; and a full App round-trip (Brain Scout -> Scout it -> Favorites -> Brain Scout) now keeps 4 .ladder-rung nodes and the typed input value intact. Full suite run clean afterward.

claim.summary:
Fix 1 (BrainScoutView.tsx MH5): `saved` was a useState initializer computed once at mount. Because scout ids hash only phrase+label (seed-independent by design), a Re-scout draw swaps in new text under the same id/React key without remounting ScoutCard, so the button stayed stuck on 'Saved ✓' while the newly displayed text was never persisted (addFavorite no-op'd on the duplicate id). Fixed by: (a) recomputing `saved` via `useEffect(() => setSaved(loadFavorites().some(f => favId(f)===id && f.kind==='scout' && f.text===text)), [id, text])` so the button reflects whether the text currently on screen is actually stored; (b) in handleSave, when addFavorite returns false (duplicate id), calling removeFavorite(id) then addFavorite again so the stale stored text gets replaced with what's displayed, instead of the click being a silent no-op. favorites.ts itself was left untouched (its no-op-on-duplicate-id contract is tested and part of the store's API).

Fix 2 (App.tsx NH1): App never wrote seed/filters back to the URL (no pushState/replaceState anywhere), so after loading a share link and then sparking or toggling a filter, location.href stayed pinned to the old params — copying the address bar shared a stale prompt, and reload silently discarded the current prompt for the old shared one. Added a `useEffect(() => { if (seed==null) return; history.replaceState(null,'',...) }, [seed, filters])` that keeps the URL's seed/subject/difficulty in sync with what's rendered, using the existing encodeShare(). Used replaceState (not pushState) so routine spark/filter interactions don't spam browser history.

Side effect fixed: App.test.tsx's beforeEach didn't reset window.location, and since jsdom's window persists across tests in a file, one test's replaceState call (from Fix 2) leaked its sparked seed/filters into the next test's initial mount, breaking the 'filter chips apply conjunctive subject + difficulty filters, empty = all' test. Added `window.history.replaceState(null, '', '/')` to beforeEach to restore test isolation — this only resets test scaffolding state, not an assertion.

Both original reproduction cases now pass (re-scout no longer shows stale 'Saved ✓' / silently drops new text; the address bar now tracks Surprise-me and filter changes). Full suite: 6 files / 116 tests, all passing.
